Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree so you don't collide with parallel work happening on this same repo right now:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-modmenu -b feature/freemc-modmenu main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-modmenu`, symlink node_modules from the primary tree if it's not already usable (`ls node_modules` — if missing/broken: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`), and symlink the env: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env` if `.env` isn't present. Do ALL your work in this worktree, not in /opt/nxeon directly.

This worktree already has a 12-mode "free Minecraft server" product on main (commit c2e97e9): one free Docker-based Minecraft server per account, on a dedicated VM ("freemc-host", a real `Server` row with `hostname="freemc-host"`), running itzg/mc-router in front of itzg/minecraft-server containers.

READ FIRST, in full: `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` and `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`. These establish every pattern you must follow:
- `FREEMC_PRESETS` in free-minecraft-control.ts: each preset has `kind: "properties" | "plugins"`, `type?: "VANILLA"|"PAPER"`, `properties` (server.properties keys), `env?` (itzg env vars, chiefly `MODRINTH_PROJECTS`/`SPIGET_RESOURCES`/`PLUGINS`, comma-separated).
- `FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION = "26.1.2"` — every plugins-kind container pins this VERSION. Do not change it or omit it for any plugin container you create — MC has moved to calendar versioning and plugin authors' builds commonly lag the newest release; 26.1.2 is the version this session hand-verified every current plugin against.
- `recreatePresetContainer` in actions-free-minecraft.ts (private helper, top of file after imports) is THE pattern for safely recreating a container: `docker rm -f` old, `docker run -d` new with merged env vars, then **critically** `sleep(15000)` followed by `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}'` before declaring success — `docker run -d`'s own exit code only means the process *started*, not that it survived (a bad plugin/version mismatch kills the container seconds later, and `docker run`'s exit code never sees that). Any new container-recreate code you write MUST follow this same health-check pattern, and must roll back to the previous working config on failure rather than leaving the customer with a dead server.
- JVM heap ratio for plugin containers is `0.7` (not 0.85 — 0.85 caused a real OOM kill on a 3-dimension SkyBlock world in live testing).
- RCON password is deterministic and never stored: `rconPasswordFor(userId)` in free-minecraft-control.ts, derived via scrypt. `sendRcon`, `readServerProperties`, `writeServerProperties`, `getFreeServerStatus`, `getFreeServerPlayers` are the existing RCON/status helpers — reuse them.
- `shellQuote` (from `lib/ssh-exec.ts`) wraps every value interpolated into a remote shell command. Never build a docker/RCON command string from unescaped/unvalidated input.
- `withServerSsh(host, async (conn) => {...})` + `exec(conn, cmd, timeoutMs)` is how every SSH command against freemc-host runs. Get the host via `db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`.

YOUR TASK — build a "Mod menu" for the free Minecraft dashboard: let an owner add EXTRA plugins on top of whatever their active preset already bundles, from a curated, vetted catalog (never free-text — a plugin slug is code executed on our infrastructure, so only ever install from a fixed allowlist you've personally verified).

1. Research a catalog of ~15-20 additional Paper/Modrinth plugins, covering a spread of categories (Economy, Protection/Anti-grief, Utility/QoL, Fun/Cosmetic, Admin/Moderation tools). Use the Modrinth API directly, e.g.:
   `curl -s "https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/<slug>/version" -H "User-Agent: research/1.0"` — confirm each candidate's latest version's `game_versions` array includes `"26.1.2"` and `loaders` includes `"paper"`. Do NOT trust API metadata alone — this session found plugins that claimed Paper 26.1.2 support but still failed at runtime (e.g. wrong download URL, missing hard dependency) or were the wrong loader entirely (a "Paper plugin" that was actually a Fabric mod). You must LIVE-TEST at least 5-6 of your chosen catalog entries against the real freemc-host before finalizing the catalog.
   AVOID duplicating anything already bundled by an existing preset: essentialsx, luckperms, vaultunlocked, towny, iridiumskyblock, lifestealz, worldedit, nochatreports-spigot-paper, hungergames-sb, ajParkour (Spiget 60909), Prison (Spiget 1223), MissileWars.

2. Live-test method: boot a bare PAPER container (VERSION=26.1.2) and layer your candidate plugins on top via `MODRINTH_PROJECTS`, same `docker run` pattern as `recreatePresetContainer`. Use container name `mc-modtest` (won't collide with other work). ENABLE_RCON=true, RCON_PASSWORD (any test value), reasonable memory (1536m container / ~1075m JVM heap for a plugins-kind test, matching this session's established ratio). Wait ~60-90s, then `docker logs mc-modtest --tail 60` and `docker inspect -f 'Running={{.State.Running}}'` to confirm a clean boot with no plugin-load errors. Clean up (`docker rm -f mc-modtest`, remove its data dir) when done, and remove any throwaway test scripts you create before finishing.

3. Build:
   - `lib/freemc-mod-catalog.ts` — exports `FREEMC_MOD_CATALOG: { slug: string; label: string; description: string; category: string }[]`, your final verified list only (drop anything that failed).
   - `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts` — `"use server"`, one action `applyFreeMinecraftMods(prev, formData)`: `requireUser()`, load the caller's `FreeMinecraftServer` row, validate every submitted slug is in `FREEMC_MOD_CATALOG` (reject anything else), refuse if the active preset's `kind !== "plugins"` (there's no plugin runtime to install into), merge the preset's own `env.MODRINTH_PROJECTS` slugs with the validated extra slugs (dedupe), recreate the container using the same health-check + rollback-on-failure discipline as `applyFreeMinecraftPreset` in actions-free-minecraft.ts (read that function for the exact rollback shape), and only persist `extraMods` on the `FreeMinecraftServer` row (already a `String[] @default([])` field in the schema — no migration needed) once the new container is confirmed running.
   - `components/customer/freemc/ModsTab.tsx` — `"use client"`, grouped-by-category checkbox grid of the catalog reflecting current `server.extraMods`, disabled with an explanatory message when the active preset is `kind:"properties"`, a "Save & restart" button wired to the action above (`useActionState`), matching the visual style of the existing `Settings`/`Overview` components in `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` (Tailwind classes, `card`/`btn-primary`/`btn-secondary` utility classes — read that file for the exact look).

4. Do NOT edit `FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, `actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, or any other existing file — only create the new files above, so your work integrates without conflicts against parallel work happening on other features right now. Do NOT merge to main or push anywhere. Do NOT delete your worktree when done — I'll integrate from it and clean it up myself.

5. Before finishing: `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` in your worktree must both pass clean. Commit your work in the worktree (git add the new files explicitly, never `git add -A`) so it's not lost.

Report back: the final catalog (with a one-line note per entry on what you verified), which ones you tested live and the result, any you dropped and why, the exact file paths you created, the worktree path/branch name, and confirmation the build/typecheck passed.

1	/**
2	 * Docker/RCON control primitives for free-tier Minecraft containers on
3	 * freemc-host — the free-tier equivalent of lib/game-control.ts, which speaks
4	 * to full Proxmox-VM game servers over SSH+tunnelled RCON. This is much
5	 * simpler: one SSH hop to the host, then `docker exec <container> ...` for
6	 * everything, using the CLI tools itzg/docker-minecraft-server already bundles
7	 * (rcon-cli, mc-monitor) instead of a hand-rolled RCON protocol client.
8	 *
9	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from both lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
10	 * and, in future, a worker sweep, same reasoning as lib/game-control.ts.
11	 */
12	import { scryptSync } from "node:crypto";
13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
15	
16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}
28	
29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}
33	
34	export type ServerStatus = {
35	  running: boolean;
36	  players: { online: number; max: number } | null;
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
52	    return { running: false, players: null };
53	  }
54	  const status = await dockerExec(
55	    conn,
56	    containerName,
57	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
58	    10_000,
59	  );
60	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
61	  try {
62	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);

#!/bin/bash
# Research helper: checks a Modrinth project slug's latest versions for
# MC 26.1.2 + paper loader support. Throwaway script, deleted before finishing.
for slug in "$@"; do
  echo "=== $slug ==="
  resp=$(curl -s "https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/$slug/version" -H "User-Agent: nxeon-research/1.0")
  ok=$(echo "$resp" | python3 -c "
import json, sys
try:
    versions = json.load(sys.stdin)
except Exception as e:
    print('PARSE_ERROR', e); sys.exit()
if not isinstance(versions, list) or not versions:
    print('NO_VERSIONS or 404'); sys.exit()
match = None
for v in versions:
    gv = v.get('game_versions', [])
    ld = v.get('loaders', [])
    if '26.1.2' in gv and 'paper' in ld:
        match = v
        break
if match:
    print('MATCH', match.get('version_number'), match.get('name'))
else:
    # show latest for diagnosis
    v = versions[0]
    print('NO_MATCH latest=', v.get('version_number'), 'game_versions_tail=', v.get('game_versions',[])[-5:], 'loaders=', v.get('loaders',[]))
"
)
  echo "$ok"
done

GrimAC fails because mc-image-helper's default MODRINTH_PROJECTS syntax only accepts release-type versions, but Grim only publishes alpha/beta builds — so it's rejected unless a version type filter is explicitly specified. This confirms the task's warning about relying on metadata alone: Grim isn't usable through the default syntax and would need a different dependency-download approach.

The container's total failure was traced to this single bad project entry aborting the whole mc-image-helper startup, confirming that any invalid modrinth spec kills the entire container — consistent with the established "one bad plugin kills everything" pattern, and validating the rollback design. Next I'll drop GrimAC and retest the remaining six projects together to confirm clean boots.
